sections.h2: Where does a deed get recorded in St. Clair County?
sections.html:
A deed for land in St. Clair County is recorded with the county Recorder of Deeds in Belleville, the county seat. Illinois law requires deeds, mortgages and powers of attorney to be recorded in the county where the land lies, and it voids any clause in a deed that tries to forbid recording.

Recording is what protects a buyer. Under 765 ILCS 5/30, a deed takes effect against creditors and later purchasers without notice only from the time it is filed for record. A signed deed sitting in a drawer protects nobody.

The office is open to the public Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, and it has 7 public workstations where anyone can search land records at no charge. Copies printed from those machines cost $2.00 per page.

sections.h2: What does the St. Clair County Recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The office posts two price columns, one with the RHSP surcharge and one without it. Transfer tax is added on top of the recording fee for deeds, leases and easements when it applies. The office accepts cash, check or money order, with checks made out to Recorder of Deeds.

The surcharge does not apply to several categories, including UCCs, judgments, wills, death certificates, powers of attorney, documents from state agencies, school districts, the federal government and municipalities, and re-recordings of an original document. If you cannot tell which row your paper falls under, the office asks you to call before you mail it.

sections.h2: How do I send a deed to the St. Clair County Recorder by mail?
sections.html:
Mail goes to Recorder of Deeds, PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222. Overnight couriers such as FedEx or UPS use a different street address: Recorder of Deeds, #10 Public Sq, 5th Floor, Belleville, IL 62220. A PO box will not accept a courier package, so match the carrier to the address.

Before you send a package, check each of these items:

  • The original signed and notarized deed, not a photocopy.
  • The completed Illinois transfer declaration that has to travel with every deed.
  • A check or money order payable to Recorder of Deeds for the fee in the row that fits the document, plus any transfer tax.
  • A return address, so the recorded deed has somewhere to go.

In a sale handled by a title company or attorney, the closing agent normally submits the deed and pays the fees.

sections.h2: What is the Illinois transfer tax on a St. Clair County sale?
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, as 35 ILCS 200/31-10 states. If the deed says the property passes subject to a mortgage, the unpaid mortgage balance is left out of the value used for the tax.

The recorder collects the tax. The statute allowed paper revenue stamps until December 31, 2025, and after that date counties issue electronic stamps or another electronic mark. The recorder files a return through the state's MyDec system and sends the money to the Department of Revenue by the 10th day of the following month. Because the St. Clair schedule says transfer tax is added for deeds when applicable, ask the office what applies to your deed before you mail payment.

Some deeds owe nothing. Section 31-45 lists exempt deeds, and the list includes these:

  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Deeds that confirm, correct or supplement an earlier recorded deed without added consideration.
  • Deeds of partition and tax deeds.
  • Deeds issued to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Deeds to or from a governmental body.

Some exempt deeds, such as deeds to or from a governmental body or a property exchange, still have to be filed with a declaration.

sections.h2: What is the transfer declaration and who signs it?
sections.html:
The transfer declaration is the Illinois form filed alongside the deed. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-25, it is due when the deed is presented for recording, or within 3 business days after the transfer, whichever comes first. At least one seller and one buyer sign it, or their attorneys or agents sign for them.

The form asks for the value of the property, the parcel number, the legal description, the deed date, the property address, the type of improvement, whether the parties are related, lot size and any homestead exemptions shown on the latest tax bill. The recorder may not accept a deed that arrives without a declaration containing all the requested information.

The parcel number matters again if you search the county's online index. The index search wants it written in the format 00-00-0-000-000.

sections.h2: How can I search or copy St. Clair County land records?
sections.html:
Three online routes exist, and all run on Fidlar software. The free route is AVA Search, which returns index data only (party name, recorded date range, parcel number, document number and document type) with no images.

Tapestry Eon is the pay-as-you-go service: $8.75 per index or image search and $1.00 per printed page. Viewing images is included in the search fee. Frequent users can sign up for Laredo Anywhere, with monthly plans that start at $75.00 for 0 to 250 minutes and reach $400.00 a month for unlimited minutes. Copies on Laredo are $.35 per printed page.

For paper copies, the office has its own rules:

  • Every request needs a document number or a book and page number.
  • Fewer than 10 non-certified copies can be requested by phone at 618-825-2481 or 618-825-2482, or by email.
  • Certified copies, and any request for 10 or more documents, must be mailed with a check for the full amount.
  • Standard copies cost $2.00 a page. A certified copy is priced at the original recording fee, minus the $10 surcharge where it applies.
  • A certified copy of a DD-214 is free, but only the named person, dependents, the county veterans' service officer and a few others may get one.

sections.h2: What should I know about St. Clair County before selling a house here?
sections.html:
St. Clair County lies directly east of St. Louis in the Metro East region of Southern Illinois. The county was created in 1790 and covers 674 square miles, of which 658 are land. Belleville is both the seat and the largest city. The 2020 census counted 257,400 people, and the 2025 estimate is 250,708, so the county is the ninth most populous in Illinois.

Housing here is mostly owner-occupied. The 2020 census shows 114,595 housing units, 65.1 percent of occupied ones owned and 34.9 percent rented. Cities in the county include Belleville, O'Fallon, Fairview Heights, Collinsville (partly), East St. Louis, Cahokia Heights, Mascoutah, Lebanon, Madison and Columbia (partly).

Buyers weigh commute and school district. Interstates 55, 64, 70 and 255 cross the county, 11 St. Louis MetroLink stations sit inside it, and Scott Air Force Base is inside the county. Districts with ground here include Belleville School District 118, O'Fallon Community Consolidated School District 90, Mascoutah Community Unit School District 19 and East St. Louis School District 189, plus Belleville Township High School District 201.

A sale of a St. Clair County house closes with a deed, a transfer declaration and any transfer tax, then recording. A house that needs repairs can still be sold as is for cash, and the closing agent files the paperwork with the recorder.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in St. Clair County, Illinois?
faqs.a: The county Recorder of Deeds in Belleville records them. The office accepts cash, check or money order, and recorded documents can be mailed to PO Box 543, Belleville, IL 62222.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in St. Clair County?
faqs.a: The county's printed schedule shows $55.00 for deeds with the RHSP surcharge and $36.00 without it. Transfer tax is added when it applies, so confirm the total with the office.

faqs.q: Does a St. Clair County deed need a transfer declaration?
faqs.a: Yes. Illinois requires a signed declaration with the deed, or within 3 business days of the transfer if that is earlier. Some exempt deeds still need it, so ask the office before you skip it.

faqs.q: Can I search St. Clair County land records online for free?
faqs.a: Yes, for index data. AVA Search shows names, dates, parcel numbers and document types without images. Images and printed copies cost extra through Tapestry Eon or Laredo Anywhere.

faqs.q: How much is the Illinois transfer tax?
faqs.a: The statute sets it at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. Exempt deeds, such as foreclosure deeds to a mortgage holder or deeds for under $100 in consideration, owe none.
